storage.search: Search finds these mails by header and preview. When online, TuxMail also searches on the mail server (IMAP); such hits are marked “header only”.

connection.filesOffline: You are offline. Files from the cloud are available again once there is a connection.
connection.expiredText: The server no longer knows this device. Sign in again to continue. Your local data and waiting mails are kept.
connection.passwordsNote: Mail passwords come encrypted from the server and can only be read by this device.

bar.offline: Offline: you see what was last loaded. New mails are sent when the connection is back.
bar.offlineLocal: Server not reachable. Your accounts keep working; settings will be synchronised later.
bar.expired: Sign-in expired. Your local data is kept.
bar.locked: Secret store locked: unlock it to connect to the server again.

mode.thin1: The server fetches your mail around the clock, even when this computer is off.
mode.thin2: The same state everywhere: here, in the browser and on your phone.
mode.thin3: No mail passwords on this device.
mode.thin4: Without a network: read what was last loaded and write mails for later.
mode.local1: This device fetches the mail itself and works fully offline.
mode.local2: Signatures, rules, saved searches and the view stay in step with the server.
mode.local3: Mail passwords are transferred to this device encrypted.
mode.local4: Server and device fetch separately: what you read or sort here reaches the server through the mail account.
mode.both: The web interface and the Android app keep working with both.
mode.pop3: Careful: at least one account uses POP3. If the server and this device both fetch and then delete, each side only sees part of the mail. Set one side to keep mail on the mail server.
mode.thinLocalAccounts: If you have accounts of your own on this device: they pause and come back unchanged when you disconnect.
mode.thinCache: Content for reading offline stays unencrypted on this device, like local mail; disconnecting can remove it securely.

outbox.title: Waiting for the connection
outbox.inDoubt: It is unclear whether this mail was already sent. Check the "Sent" folder before sending it again.
outbox.blocked: Not sent: the send checks want you to look at this.
outbox.conflictGone: Not done: the mail no longer exists on the server. It was deleted or moved there in the meantime.
outbox.conflictRefused: Not done: the server refused this action. Check the mail once there is a connection again.
outbox.blockedToast: A waiting mail was not sent: the send checks want you to look at it.
outbox.discardedSent: The mail was sent although you discarded it: it was already on its way.
outbox.discardedUnclear: Discarded, but perhaps already sent: the mail was on its way when you discarded it. Check "Sent".
outbox.discardedNotSent: Discarded. The mail was not sent.

log.title: Synchronisation log
log.conflict: (changed on both sides: the newer state applies)
log.skipped: "{name}" not transferred: it refers to something that does not exist on the other side
log.error: "{name}" could not be synchronised this time

leave.title: Disconnect from {server}?
leave.device: This device is signed out at the server and its sign-in data here is deleted.
leave.server: Everything on the server stays: accounts, mail, calendars, contacts.
leave.local: Accounts of your own on this device and their mail stay too, and run by themselves again.
leave.deleteCache: Delete content stored for reading offline ({size})
leave.outbox: {count} actions are still waiting and could not be sent. They are lost when you disconnect.
leave.outbox_one: {count} action is still waiting and could not be sent. It is lost when you disconnect.
leave.notRevoked: The server could not be reached, so this device is still in its device list. Remove it in the web interface under Security > Sessions. The sign-in data on this device has been deleted.

connection.adminBrowser: Server administration is only available in the browser.
connection.attention: Something from the sync with the server is waiting for your decision.

rules.why: Rules can forward or delete mail. What comes from the server stays off here until you have seen it.
rules.wasOn: Was switched on and is now off because of this.
rules.external: Acts outside TuxMail, for example by forwarding.

unclear.text: The mail may already have been sent. Check the Sent folder first.
